title: Fast and Accurate Online Coupled Matrix-Tensor Factorization via Frequency Regularization

problem.claim: Efficiently and accurately factorizing multi-source data in dynamic and real-time environments is a central problem.

gap.claim: Existing CMTF methods face scalability and computational-efficiency limitations for continuously streaming data, require retraining as new data arrive, and often fail to incorporate inherent temporal characteristics.

narrative_sequence.summary: The source frames efficient and accurate factorization of dynamic multi-source data as the research question.
CMTF is presented as a powerful tool, but existing methods struggle with scalability for continuously streaming data.
Traditional CMTF approaches are described as computationally inefficient and dependent on retraining when new data arrive.
Many techniques do not properly incorporate temporal characteristics that could improve accuracy and convergence speed.

source_observation.claim: Streaming settings expose scalability, retraining, and temporal-modeling limitations in conventional factorization methods.

interpretation.claim: Online methods may need to address computational cost and temporal structure jointly.

application.claim: When designing real-time multi-source factorization systems, consider incremental updates and explicit temporal characteristics.
